The offline block patches only the `httpx` distribution, but `anthropic==1.3.0` does not use `httpx` — it depends on `httpx2<3,>=2.0.0` (resolved to httpx2 2.12.0 in the committed uv.lock, line 217). `anthropic._base_client.SyncHttpxClientWrapper` is an `httpx2.Client` whose transport is `httpx2.HTTPTransport`, a completely different class from the patched `httpx.HTTPTransport`. Every Anthropic SDK call made from inside the test suite therefore goes straight to the real api.anthropic.com. This directly violates SPEC C7 ("no test may hit the network") and falsifies the conftest docstring's claim that "nothing can reach a socket". Blast radius is T-2, which ships the real `LLMClient` on this SDK and whose acceptance includes a conformance test over the real client; `config.Settings` loads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `.env`, so an accidental real-client construction in any later ticket spends the owner's key and makes the suite nondeterministic and non-offline. Fix: also monkeypatch `httpx2.HTTPTransport.handle_request` and `httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport.handle_async_request` (both attributes exist, verified). Note starlette's TestClient is also an `httpx2.Client`, so the repo now has two HTTP stacks and only one is guarded.

defect: THE TASTE CLASSIFIER TRUSTS THE MODEL'S ECHO OF fact_id, AND AN R11 SENTENCE CAN BE DISPLAYED AS A RESULT. defect: A real text page in a legacy encoding served WITHOUT a charset header is discarded as binary, and then negatively cached for 900s with its body thrown away. httpx decodes with default_encoding='utf-8' when the header carries no charset (it never reads <meta charset>), so the bytes become U+FFFD and looks_binary rejects the page against MAX_UNDECODABLE_RATIO = 0.10. MEASURED U+FFFD density on natural prose, not cherry-picked accents: Japanese Shift-JIS 64.9%, EUC-JP 65.2%, Chinese GBK/GB18030 76.4%, Czech iso-8859-2 13.70%, Turkish iso-8859-9 11.55% — ALL DROPPED. Western European latin-1 (French 5.12%, Spanish 5.28%, German 4.31%, Portuguese 3.49%) survives, so the code comment's claim of 'room on both sides' is true only for the languages it was tested against. Worse than 'no document': _remember_non_text discards the body too, so a caller wanting raw bytes loses them. Fix: decide binary-ness from the BYTES, not from a decode known to have used the wrong codec — either pass default_encoding=<detector callable> to the httpx.AsyncClient at client.py:260, or when the declared type is textual and looks_binary fires, re-decode response.content using a BOM/<meta charset> sniff and re-test before rejecting.

Same page WITH charset declared -> a RawDoc whose text head reads correctly. Reproduced end-to-end by the cycle-5 adversarial verifier.

A real French sample measures 9.813%, one percentage point from the cliff; Czech, Turkish and every CJK legacy encoding cross it. Fix: replace the transliterated body with real accented prose whose density approaches the threshold, and add a CJK case.

A company with a .com plus a .io, .co.uk or GitHub-Pages docs site is common and one document each is the common case, so the refusal fires on ordinary input. The order-independence invariant DOES hold (verified over all 120 permutations of a 5-document corpus, 1 distinct answer) — the problem is what the set is scored on. defect: A single-word hub label ending in -s, -ed or -ing SILENTLY DELETES a Meet row's reasoning. Traced through the real path (digest._speakable_match), not just the predicate: 'Both connected to Databricks.' -> 'Worth a hello; nothing quotable on the record yet.'; 'Both connected to Reuters.' -> BLANKED; 'Both building on Kubernetes.' -> BLANKED; 'Both deep in Sailing.' -> BLANKED. The _reads_as_a_verb docstring anticipates the FACT case ('...at Reuters on the data team') and calls rejection 'the safe direction', which is right for a fact — it falls through to the next candidate — but WRONG for a why, where the fallback is not another candidate but an admitted blank. The fix belongs in digest, not graph: a hub label arriving through _WHY_PHRASE is a noun BY CONSTRUCTION, so the why path can tell the verb detector so. Fixing it from graph would mean rewording templates to dodge a downstream heuristic, coupling the two modules and colliding with test_why_phrasing_varies_by_hub_type. Two stale references to fold in while there: digest.py:~337's _reads_as_a_verb docstring and tests/digest/test_t7_grammar_and_order.py:141 both cite 'Both deep in Developer-tools go-to-market.' as graph's output, which T-041 has now lower-cased.

defect: SPEC C5 says 'Wikidata <= a few CONCURRENT' and the system has no concurrency cap at all — only a rate. HostRateLimiter is a GCRA token bucket: it schedules ARRIVAL TIMES and never observes a completion, so nothing in it bounds requests in flight, and no value in HOST_RATE_PER_SEC can become one. T-076 set wikimedia hosts to 1.0/s as the closest available approximation (deliberately below the published 5/s, because burst is rate*2 capped at 8, so 5.0 would permit 8 in flight against a host asking for 1) — but a per-second rate is not a concurrency cap and the green on that ticket must not be read as C5 being honoured. Fix: an asyncio.Semaphore held ACROSS the request in http/client.py, per host, sized from a new HOST_CONCURRENCY map. Roughly ten lines, but it changes that module's shape, which is why the T-076 lane correctly declined to do it inside a ticket about a missing table entry.
